text: Definition 4 (Abstract Decision Problem) assumes the label is a deterministic function of the input, the prover always argues for label 1 and chooses a mapping from inputs to messages, the verifier chooses a convex combination of base verifiers, both policy sets include every constant mapping, and there exists a deterministic verifier policy v* in the verifier's class that is complete: for some prover policy p in the prover class, v*(x, p(x)) = f(x) for every input x.
title: Abstract decision problem assumptions: deterministic labels and a complete verifier
